novel_features.name: Snapshot ledger
novel_features.description: Keep a local, timestamped ledger of readiness reports and their provenance.
novel_features.rationale: The service exposes the latest stored report, but only a local store can preserve each observation and distinguish service scan time from fetch time.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Choose this when you need an auditable local timeline instead of one ephemeral API response.

novel_features.name: Cross-report diff
novel_features.description: See which readiness scores and findings changed between two retained audits.
novel_features.rationale: A diff requires two locally retained snapshots and normalized issue identity; no single API response can provide that comparison.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Choose this after a deployment to verify whether agent-readiness regressions were introduced or fixed.

novel_features.name: Explainable policy gate
novel_features.description: Fail CI with an explicit, machine-readable readiness policy decision.
novel_features.rationale: Teams define their own score, tier, and regression policy over report data; the service only returns evidence, not repository-specific acceptance rules.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Choose this when a release pipeline must enforce readiness instead of merely displaying it.

novel_features.name: Portfolio matrix
novel_features.description: Compare a fleet of public sites in one sortable score and issue matrix.
novel_features.rationale: The API is one-target-per-request, while a local orchestrator can fetch, cache, deduplicate, and aggregate targets under the published quota.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Choose this for platform or agency work spanning multiple public targets.

novel_features.name: Issue lifecycle queue
novel_features.description: Track when readiness findings first appeared, last appeared, were fixed, or regressed.
novel_features.rationale: Lifecycle state emerges only by joining issue IDs across retained snapshots; the current report has no temporal issue history.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Choose this to turn recurring findings into a remediation queue with honest history.

novel_features.name: Rate-aware fleet scheduler
novel_features.description: Refresh many targets with bounded concurrency, deduplication, and Retry-After-aware pacing.
novel_features.rationale: Quota-aware scheduling and resumable fleet state are client concerns missing from the one-target API and official CLI.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Choose this for repeatable fleet refreshes that must respect the public 120-per-minute quota.

novel_features.name: Evidence bundle
novel_features.description: Package a report and its provenance into a portable evidence artifact.
novel_features.rationale: A local export can combine raw report data, observation time, stable URL, and comparison context for tickets or release records.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Choose this when an audit must travel with a review, ticket, or release artifact.

narrative.headline: Turn Is Agentic reports into durable, scriptable readiness evidence.
narrative.value_prop: Retrieve the official report with the same read-only contract as the upstream CLI, then keep local history, diffs, fleet comparisons, policy gates, issue lifecycles, and exportable evidence beside it. The API remains the source of truth; the local layer makes repeated engineering work compound.

quickstart.comment: Verify the generated CLI and public-service configuration without network access.
Preview the canonical report request safely.
Fetch the latest completed report as structured JSON.

troubleshoots.fix: Open the canonical report URL printed in the error, start the scan there, then retry the CLI.
Honor Retry-After and lower portfolio concurrency or max requests.
Retry without launching a new scan; the service may be refreshing stored evidence.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent or engineering workflow needs an Is Agentic score, evidence-backed issues, or repeatable comparisons across public sites. Prefer the local history, diff, portfolio, and check commands when the task spans deployments or more than one target.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI as a security, accessibility, compliance, or penetration-test substitute.
Do not use it for private or authenticated pages that the public scan cannot observe.
Do not use it to start arbitrary scans through undocumented website internals; start a missing scan from the official web report page.
